issues.item: Memory: Verbal Access: I can talk about what happened very easily.
issues.explanation: Within the Memory node, 'I can talk about what happened very easily' conflicts with the co-occurring memory profile of intrusive, disorganised trauma memory ('the memory forces its way into my mind' and 'I cannot put the memories ... in the right order'), especially in a severe PTSD presentation after terrorism. Although not impossible, this combination is clinically hard to reconcile as the same patient's dominant trauma-memory style.

'Having difficulty concentrating' is not a threat appraisal/perception item and is weakly connected to the rest of the selected threat content ('false alarms', 'waking to check safety'). It reads more like a general arousal/cognitive symptom than a threat representation, making this item poorly aligned with the Threat component and the formulation pattern linking triggers with perceived danger.

issues.item: Memory: Verbal Access: I can talk about what happened very easily.
issues.explanation: Within Memory, 'I can talk about what happened very easily' conflicts with 'the memory forces its way into my mind when I do not want it to' and 'I cannot put the memories of the event in the right order.' In severe PTSD after terrorism, intrusive and disorganized trauma memory usually does not coherently pair with very easy voluntary verbal access; this suggests opposing memory states.

Within Threat, 'Having difficulty concentrating' is not a threat appraisal item and does not cohere with the other two threat items ('false alarms' and 'waking to check safety'), which both reflect perceived ongoing danger. It appears to describe a general symptom rather than threat-specific cognitions, weakening internal consistency of the Threat node.

issues.item: Memory: Verbal Access: I can talk about what happened very easily.
issues.explanation: The memory profile is internally strained: 'I can talk about what happened very easily' sits awkwardly with severe PTSD plus 'the memory forces its way into my mind' and 'I cannot put the memories in the right order.' Easy voluntary narration is not impossible, but in this context it is hard to reconcile with such marked intrusive and disorganized remembering.

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Inaction Guilt: I will never forgive myself for not doing more to stop what happened
issues.explanation: The appraisal pattern suggests strong self-blame for personal action/inaction during the event ('not doing more to stop what happened'; 'I acted in ways that go against who I am'). For a terrorism trauma, these can occur, but paired with the rest of the profile they imply a substantial perpetrator/responsibility role that is not supported elsewhere by the triggers, threat, or memory items.
